newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AVIS PLANS RIGHS ISSUE FOR GROWTH, CUT DEBT.
newsitem.headline: AVIS PLANS RIGHS ISSUE FOR GROWTH, CUT DEBT.

text.p: South African tourism and car rental firm Avis Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it would raise more funds to help cut its gearing and fund further expansion through an issue of shares in the next few months.
Avis said it was also actively involved in investigating the acquisition or grassroots development of businesses designed to extend its presence in the Southern African tourism market.
"Following Avis's successful listing in April and its strong set of maiden results, the group would seek to raise further funds in the next few months through an offer of shares.
"The proceeds of this exercise would be used to reduce gearing further and to finance expansion," chairman Peet van der Walt said in the annual report for the year to March 31.
He said the company's gearing ratio of 1.9 was well within its comfort zone.

Avis in May reported a rise in attributable income in the year to 44.5 million rand from 34.6 million rand previously. Headline earnings per share rose to 35.95 cents from 27.50 cents in the previous year.

The general reduction in used car values and introduction of new lower priced models negatively affected the group. He said the real impact was in holding cost of vehicles rather than in lower used car prices.

Van der Walt said, however, the firm would post a rise in earnings in the current financial year as it continued to benefit from an increase in inbound travel to southern Africa and the outsourcing of fleet management.
"With all its businesses units budgeting for growth, the Avis group should produce a further real increase in earnings per share for the year to March, 1998," van der Walt said.
Avis is also listed in the Namibia and Botswana bourses and has interests in car sales, body shops and coach tours.

It has a presence through most of Southern Africa where it operates in Botswana, Namibia and Swaziland and manages Avis sub-licensees in Angola, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
